rationale: ϣϭⲁ (Lyc.) appears twice on this page (lines 1, 14) paired with πληγή 'plague/blow' as the bodily affliction-pair. Likely related to a wound/cut root. Distinct from ⲡⲱⲍ ('wound/breach') and ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ ('plague/blow') — the trio designates different aspects of bodily injury.

Reading as ϣⲱⲱⲥ 'blame, contempt' rather than the homophone ϣⲱⲥ 'shepherd' (in glossary). Pairs antithetically with ⲡⲉⲁⲩ 'glory' in the rhetorical doublet 'glory and shame of the body' that the tongue proclaims.

Variant of ⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ/ⲙ̄ⲧⲟⲛ 'rest' with ⲥ-prefix. Used here in 'concerning her purification and her healing... and the rest [ⲡⲥⲙⲧⲁⲛ]' — the soteriological refreshment/rest brought by Jesus the Radiance to the wounded living soul.
Already in glossary as ⲡⲓⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'this manner.' This page confirms ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ as bare form: ⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ ⲍⲱⲱϩ 'in the manner likewise' (line 1).
Lyc. term for river-flood, possibly cognate with ⲏⲙⲏⲣⲉ/ⲙⲣⲱ. Used here for the great Tigris flood in Pharmouthi that drove the lions over the embankment into the city. Topographic-cosmographic term.
Greek loanword κρηπίς 'embankment, quay, breastwork.' The constructed bank at the Tigris where Mani stood after his audience with Shapur.
The river of Mesopotamia. Standard transliteration of Greek Τίγρις. The Sasanian capital Ctesiphon lay on the Tigris; Mani's encounters with Shapur take place in this geographical setting.
Coptic transliteration of Greek Σαπώρης rendering Middle Persian Šābuhr / Šāpūr. Sasanian king (240-270 CE) who patronized Mani. Cf. accumulated vocabulary entry ⲁⲣⲧⲁⲝⲟⲟⲥ for his father Ardashir I.
Coptic ⲉⲃⲟⲧ/ⲉⲃⲁⲧ 'month.' Used in standard date-formulas: 'it was the month of Pharmouthi' (line 28-29).
Coptic ⲕⲣⲟ 'shore, bank, edge.' Riverside-locale term distinct from ⲕⲣⲏⲡⲓⲥ (embankment/quay structure).
